questions.stem: Consider the following about GOODS AND SERVICES TAX (GST). 1. It subsumed Central excise, service tax, VAT, entry tax, octroi, and many cesses. 2. GST is a destination-based tax. 3. The GST Council is chaired by the Finance Minister and votes follow a weighted system. 4. Petrol, diesel, ATF, crude oil and natural gas are PROVISIONALLY outside the GST net. Which are correct?
questions.explanation: All four correct. GST effective 1 July 2017 via 101st Amendment. Destination-based (tax accrues to consuming state). GST Council — FM chairs; 1/3 weight to Centre, 2/3 total to all States. Petroleum products are constitutionally included but kept OUTSIDE the GST net by Council decision — to be added later.

questions.stem: NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission in which year?
questions.explanation: NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) constituted on 1 January 2015 by a Cabinet resolution, replacing the 1950-established Planning Commission. PM is ex-officio chairperson; Vice-Chairman and CEO appointed by PM. Not a constitutional body.

questions.stem: A government runs a FISCAL DEFICIT of 5% of GDP. Which of the following statements is/are correct? 1. The fiscal deficit equals the sum of revenue deficit and capital expenditure. 2. Primary deficit = Fiscal deficit − Interest payments. 3. A higher fiscal deficit, financed by borrowing, tends to increase public debt as a % of GDP over time. 4. In India, FRBM Act targets a fiscal deficit of 3% of GDP under normal conditions.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is WRONG as a definition. Fiscal deficit = total expenditure − total revenue (excluding borrowings). It is NOT 'revenue deficit + capital expenditure' — that conflates different concepts. The other three are correct: primary deficit subtracts interest payments; higher fiscal deficit → higher debt; FRBM (2003, amended 2018) targets 3% of GDP normally.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a BRETTON WOODS institution?

options.option_text: International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (World Bank)

questions.explanation: ADB was founded in 1966 (Manila) separately. Bretton Woods (1944, New Hampshire) created IMF and the World Bank (originally IBRD; IDA is now a part of the WB Group). The ITO was proposed but never formed — its successor is the WTO (1995).

questions.stem: ASSERTION (A): India's CURRENT ACCOUNT DEFICIT (CAD) is widened by persistent crude-oil imports. REASON (R): India imports over 80% of its crude oil requirements, exposing the current account to oil-price shocks.

options.option_text: Both A and R are true, R is the correct explanation
Both A and R are true, R is NOT the correct explanation
A is true, R is false
A is false, R is true

questions.explanation: India imports ~85% of its crude. A $10/barrel rise in crude adds roughly $15 bn to the annual oil import bill. This directly widens the merchandise trade deficit and thus the CAD. Classic textbook vulnerability — reflected in every Economic Survey.

questions.stem: The PRADHAN MANTRI JAN DHAN YOJANA (PMJDY) was launched in:
questions.explanation: PMJDY launched on 28 August 2014 — financial-inclusion scheme, zero-balance accounts, RuPay debit card, accident insurance. Over 50 crore accounts opened by 2024.
